take.thing: On the product card the name sits left and a row of fabric dots sits right of it, with the price under the name.
take.why: The shopper sees there is a fabric choice before opening the piece, a cheap front door to Build yours.

left_out: the eyebrow line above the headline
differences: Dots open the Build yours section on that fabric
Our cards sit on ivory not grey
Price sits on the button row not under the name
sources.removal: The card hides that a fabric choice exists.

take.thing: The cut out piece sits large on a plain ground with a macro of its fabric running off the cropped screen edge.
take.why: It shows the weave a buyer will touch, which a flat colour dot never can.

left_out: the three crops along the bottom
differences: The macro appears only when a dot is pressed
The ground is ivory not white
One card, not a full sheet
sources.removal: Fabric becomes a flat dot and buyers cannot judge texture.

take.thing: Each card reads the piece name, one material line, then price and the Buy button on the same row.
take.why: It answers can I afford this beside the action, so the visitor decides without scrolling.

left_out: the star scores and tag chips
the giant wordmark with the chair
differences: The material line sits under a serif name
The button is WhatsApp not a cart
sources.removal: The price drifts away from the button and the card turns into a gallery.
